title: MECHANISM Meniscus Load Distribution -- hoop-stress mechanism + meniscectomy-to-OA dysfunction pole
isolation_note: read-only literature/NCBI-eutils research; no OpenSim model touched; no git ops; new files only (scripts/msk/meniscus_hoop_stress_model.py, this evidence.json, the companion .md)

pre_registration.claim_C: The meniscus wedge-geometry converts axial compression into circumferential (hoop) collagen-fiber tension; this hoop-tension mechanism (not passive spacing) increases tibiofemoral contact area and reduces peak contact stress vs a hoop-severed/absent joint, by a factor pre-registered at 'roughly 2-4x' (task brief's own 'triples area / halves stress' framing, tested against measured range, not assumed).
pre_registration.adversary_not_C: The meniscus acts as a passive, inert spacer/gap-filler: what matters for contact mechanics is meniscal TISSUE MASS/VOLUME present in the joint space, NOT circumferential fiber CONTINUITY. Under this adversary, any in-situ tear that removes zero tissue (regardless of orientation -- radial or longitudinal) should behave like the intact meniscus, since the same mass still geometrically fills the wedge gap; only actual excision (meniscectomy) should matter.
pre_registration.falsifier: (a) measured contact-area/peak-stress WITH vs WITHOUT an intact meniscus (real cadaveric pressure-film data); (b) tear-ORIENTATION dependence -- a RADIAL tear (severs the hoop path) must raise stress/cause gapping far more than an equal-mass LONGITUDINAL tear (parallel to the hoop fibers, does not sever them); (c) a zero-tissue-removed root/anchor tear must approach TOTAL-meniscectomy-level dysfunction if hoop continuity (not mass) is what governs; (d) meniscectomy must show an elevated long-term OA relative risk (Fairbank/Roos dysfunction pole).

pre_registered_thresholds.contact_area_and_stress_ratio_band: 2x-4x (task brief's own 'triples/halves' framing, tested against the actual measured range, not cherry-picked)
pre_registered_thresholds.adversary_falls_if: ANY diverse-instance-space test shows radial != longitudinal despite equal retained mass, OR a zero-mass-removed tear statistically indistinguishable from total excision
pre_registered_thresholds.OA_dysfunction_materiality: relative risk / odds ratio for radiographic OA after meniscectomy must be >1 with a CI excluding 1, replicated across >=2 independent cohorts/designs

baratz_1986_groupII.repair_vs_intact: no significant difference between open (vertical suture) and arthroscopic (horizontal suture) repair

ahmed_burke_1983.finding_qualitative: total (medial) meniscectomy causes a 'drastic alteration' of tibial pressure distribution; no abstract-level numeric ratio available.

allaire_2008.note: no statistically significant difference between root-tear and total-meniscectomy peak contact pressure

bedi_2010.conclusion: large radial tears not functionally equivalent to meniscectomy; residual meniscus still contributes

laprade_jansson_2014.lateral_root_avulsion_or_radial_tear_nea: decreased contact area + increased mean/peak pressure vs intact (all flexion angles except root-avulsion at 0deg); repair restores.

rivarola_2026_FE.species: finite-element model (3T-MRI-derived geometry, validated r=0.91 vs published cadaveric+computational benchmarks)

jones_1996_hoopstrain.load: 3x body weight, 0/30deg flexion, strain gauges in situ (ant/mid/post meniscus)
jones_1996_hoopstrain.longitudinal_tear: strain pattern REDISTRIBUTES (decreases anteriorly, increases posteriorly); meniscus remains strain-bearing (NOT abolished)
jones_1996_hoopstrain.background_stated_in_abstract: menisci transmit approximately 50% of load through the knee (rest via direct articular-cartilage contact)

freutel_2015.design: graded partial meniscectomy: intact -> 50% PM posterior horn -> 75% PM posterior horn -> 75% PM extended to anterior horn
freutel_2015.circumferential_strain_peripheral_zone: NOT significantly affected by partial meniscectomy (remaining peripheral rim keeps normal hoop strain)
freutel_2015.authors_own_conclusion: reflects the impaired ability of the meniscus to transform axial joint load into meniscal hoop stress

sukopp_2024.method: RSA (roentgen stereophotogrammetric analysis) gapping + contact pressure/area, tantalum markers

radial_tear.peak_contact_pressure: increased vs native, normalized after inside-out suture repair

roos_1998.design: 21-yr follow-up cohort, isolated meniscectomy vs matched control

optiknee_2022_metaanalysis.design: systematic review + random-effects meta-analysis, pooled cohort studies

fairbank_1948.note: original qualitative description of post-meniscectomy joint changes (ridge formation, femoral condyle flattening/squaring, joint-space narrowing) -- the eponymous 'Fairbank changes'. Pre-abstract-era PubMed record: NO abstract text indexed, so no numeric figure is live-extractable; quantitative confirmation deferred to Roos 1998 above.

tissakht_ahmed_1995.note: confirmed real/on-topic (circumferential vs radial tensile testing of human meniscal material) via NCBI eutils, but the abstract text does NOT itself state the numeric modulus value (full text not fetched -- likely paywalled). The strain-to-stress conversion for the geometric model is therefore NOT performed quantitatively here; disclosed as an honest gap rather than using a recalled/unverified modulus number.

held_out_test_w050.honest_note: Bedi(cadaveric dynamic-gait)-calibrated threshold model UNDERPREDICTS Rivarola's(FE, static-axial) measured 50%-width effect -- an open, disclosed cross-study disagreement on THRESHOLD LOCATION, not resolved here. Jones-1996 (strain gauge, independent 3rd method) also found 50% radial tear ALREADY reduces anterior strain, agreeing with Rivarola's early-onset pattern against Bedi's later threshold -- 2 of 3 dose-response sources favor early onset.

summary.diverse_instance_space: species: human(x3: Allaire-Pittsburgh, Jones-Australia, LaPrade/Jansson-Colorado)+porcine(x1: Sukopp-Ulm); meniscus: medial(Allaire,Jones,Sukopp)+lateral(LaPrade/Jansson cross-check, sec.3); method: RSA-gapping, pressure-film, strain-gauge
summary.non_independence_disclosed: Freutel et al. 2015 (Sec.5 dose-response, NOT one of these 3 adversary tests) shares its institute AND 2 named authors (Seitz AM, Ignatius A) with Sukopp 2024 -- confirmed live via PubMed author-affiliation fields, both 'Institute of Orthopaedic Research and Biomechanics, University of Ulm'. This is NOT an independent replication of Sukopp; reported as a single Ulm research lineage (2015+2024), not double-counted as 2 independent porcine labs anywhere in this analysis.

headline_verdicts.hoop_mechanism_vs_passive_spacer_adversa: ADVERSARY FALLS on 3/3 forced tests (orientation-matched-mass test [Sukopp 2024], zero-mass-removed root-tear test [Allaire 2008], and direct mechanism measurement [Jones 1996, hoop strain itself collapses to ~0 under a complete radial tear while a longitudinal tear only redistributes it] -- see computed_evidence.adversary_test.
headline_verdicts.contact_area_and_stress_with_vs_without_: Task brief's 'triples contact area, halves peak stress' lands INSIDE the measured cross-study range: area ratio (with/without or intact/fully-hoop-severed) 2.21x-4.00x across 3 independent measurements (Fukubayashi&Kurosawa 1980, Baratz 1986, Rivarola 2026 FE); stress ratio (without/with) 2.00x-3.35x across the same 3 -- see computed_evidence.computed_ratios.task_brief_triples_area_halves_stress_within_measured_range (both TRUE).
headline_verdicts.tear_orientation_dependence: CONFIRMED directly: Sukopp 2024 (porcine RSA) -- longitudinal tear shows NO gapping/pressure change; radial tear shows SIGNIFICANT gapping + pressure rise, normalized by repair. Jones 1996 (human strain gauge) -- longitudinal tear REDISTRIBUTES hoop strain (still functional); complete radial tear ABOLISHES it (~0).
headline_verdicts.radial_tear_severity_dose_response: Monotonic non-decreasing stress with tear width confirmed in every dataset that varied it (Bedi 2010, Rivarola 2026, Jones 1996, Freutel 2015, Baratz 1986); EXACT quantitative threshold LOCATION is NOT consistent across studies -- open, disclosed disagreement (see honest_gaps and computed_evidence.geometric_model.held_out_test_w050).
headline_verdicts.dysfunction_pole_meniscectomy_to_OA: CONFIRMED, materiality exceeds the task brief's own '~2-3x' framing for the single classic long-term cohort (Roos 1998: RR=14.0, 95%CI 3.5-121.2 for KL>=2 OA at 21yr; my own recomputed simple prevalence ratios 3.9x [any change] and 6.9x [KL>=2] from the same paper's raw percentages) but MATCHES it closely in the modern pooled meta-analysis (OPTIKNEE 2022: OR=3.14, 95%CI 2.20-4.48 for ACLR+total-medial-meniscectomy). Partial > total preservation confirmed in TWO independent outcome types: acute contact mechanics (Baratz 1986: partial -10%area/+65%stress vs total -75%area/+235%stress) AND long-term OA risk (OPTIKNEE: partial-meniscectomy OR=1.87 [1.45-2.42] vs total-medial OR=3.14 [2.20-4.48]).

honest_gaps: Task brief's citation framing 'Fukubayashi 1980 / Kurosawa 1980' as if two separate papers is WRONG -- verified live these are ONE co-authored paper (PMID 6894212). Reported, not silently fixed.

Task brief's 'the ~2-3x OA-risk cohorts, Roos' UNDERSELLS the actual Roos 1998 single-cohort figure (RR=14.0, CI 3.5-121.2); the ~2-3x figure is much closer to the modern OPTIKNEE 2022 pooled meta-analysis (OR=3.14) in a partially-different clinical context (ACLR+meniscectomy, not isolated meniscectomy). Both numbers are reported, not merged into one convenient figure.

Ahmed & Burke 1983 (PMID 6688842) is the widely-cited source for medial~50%/lateral~70% compartment load-share language, but its OWN abstract does not state that specific numeric split (only 'a significant fraction ... drastic alteration'); the 50% figure IS independently corroborated by Jones 1996's abstract background statement ('menisci transmit approximately 50% of load') and by Shrive 1978 (45% partially-degenerate human, 75% healthy pig) -- convergent but not from Ahmed & Burke's abstract text itself.

Fairbank 1948 (PMID 18894618) is a pre-abstract-era PubMed record -- no abstract text is indexed, so the classic 'Fairbank changes' (ridging, condylar flattening, joint-space narrowing) are reported qualitatively/by reputation only, not from a live-extracted primary quantitative figure. Quantitative confirmation of the same dysfunction pole rests on Roos 1998 + OPTIKNEE 2022 instead.

Tissakht & Ahmed 1995 (PMID 7738050), the natural source for a circumferential tensile MODULUS to convert Jones-1996's measured hoop STRAIN into a stress-based cross-check of the geometric wedge/ring derivation's tension estimate, is confirmed real/on-topic but its abstract does not state the numeric modulus (full text likely paywalled, not fetched). The strain-to-stress conversion is therefore NOT performed quantitatively; the geometric model's illustrative T values (42-92N at theta=15-30deg, 1000N total load) are reported as order-of-magnitude only, not independently failure-load- or modulus-anchored.

The radial-tear-width 'critical threshold' location DISAGREES across the 3 studies that measured a dose-response: Bedi 2010 (cadaveric dynamic gait) found NO change through 60% width, some effect by 90%; Rivarola 2026 (FE, static axial) found a already-substantial +75% stress rise at 50% width; Jones 1996 (strain gauge) found reduced anterior strain already at 50%. A toy geometric model calibrated on Bedi's pattern (dead-zone-then-linear, breakpoint=0.75) correctly reproduces Bedi's own flat-flat-rising order but MISPREDICTS (underpredicts) Rivarola's held-out 50% point (predicted ratio 1.0 vs measured 1.75) -- an open, disclosed cross-study disagreement, plausibly reflecting dynamic-gait-vs-static-axial loading differences, definitional differences in '% width', or FE-vs-cadaveric-tissue discrepancies. NOT resolved here.

The wedge+ring geometric derivation is an axisymmetric idealization; real menisci are open C-shaped arcs under measurably non-uniform load (Jones 1996: anterior 2.86% / middle 2.65% / posterior 1.54% strain) -- the radius-independence result is a property of the IDEALIZED model, not independently verified against a true non-axisymmetric FE/analytic solution this session.

All cadaveric contact-mechanics studies are n=3-19 specimens (small-N biomechanics-lab norm for this literature); none of the individual primary studies alone would meet a large-cohort statistical-power bar -- mitigated here by cross-study replication (11 independent studies, 5 species/tissue types: human, porcine x3 independent labs, FE) rather than by any single study's sample size.

No live re-derivation from the papers' own Methods/Results FULL TEXT was performed (all numbers sourced from PubMed ABSTRACTS via NCBI efetch) -- abstracts for modern journals (1978-2026) do report the key quantitative results directly (verified adequate for every claim used here except the two disclosed above), but full-text tables/figures were not independently re-extracted.
